prompt: State what is meant by an elastic collision.
hints: Focus on the specific physical quantity that is conserved in an elastic collision but not in an inelastic collision.
solution: An elastic collision is a collision in which the total kinetic energy of the system is the same before and after the collision (or total kinetic energy is conserved).
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Recall the definition of elastic collision from Cambridge 9702.
Step 2: State clearly that total kinetic energy is conserved / remains the same before and after the collision.

mark_scheme.criterion: Total kinetic energy is conserved / total kinetic energy before collision equals total kinetic energy after collision
